idea-plugin.name: Cinder Memory
idea-plugin.description:
The local-first memory layer for AI coding agents.
Ask your Cinder knowledge base a question from inside the IDE and read the answer with its sources, without leaving the editor.
Cinder keeps what your coding agents learn — why a decision was made, what gotcha you hit, what to do next — in a local, searchable store. This plugin is the console for it:
• A conversation, not a result list: you ask a question, the turn joins the feed, and the turns stay there. The newest two stay open; older ones fold into one row and open on click, so "what did I just ask" is always one click away. • Three knowledge faces, one keystroke apart: Ask answers with prose and a folded "Sources" list, Notes brings up your notes and todos, Pages brings up the approved knowledge pages. A note or a page opens IN PLACE, inside the turn that produced it. • Locked to your project by default: the chip next to the modes shows which project the panel is scoped to, and clicking it puts the panel back to cross-project. Ask and Pages really filter server-side; Notes cannot (the tool has no project parameter), so the panel filters the hits itself and tells you how many it dropped. A folder that is not in the knowledge base yet says so and offers the projects it could belong to — one click files it. • Your own AI provider, configured where settings live: the gear in the panel header opens Cinder's settings, and "AI Provider" is its own page there — endpoint, key and model, written to the local Cinder service, the same settings the desktop app uses, so the two never disagree. "Fetch models" asks the endpoint what it offers; "Test" proves the answer comes back before you save. • Full-text search (FTS5) over every note and todo you ever captured, ranked exactly as the Cinder Desktop app ranks it — the plugin reimplements no ranking, no snippet extraction, no gating. • Nothing to leave the editor for: a card opens in place, and "Ask about this" asks about that exact item — the question goes into the composer and is sent, so the follow-up is the next turn in the same feed. • One settings tree, not two: the gear opens Cinder's settings — the cinder-mcp binary with a "Check MCP channel" report that lists every place it looked, the optional local service with "Test connection" and "Start local service", and the AI provider on its own page. • Note maintenance without leaving the IDE: edit a note's title, kind, tags and 项目 (project), add a new note under the same 项目, or let the AI tidy a note into a restructured proposal — sections, an index, and a mermaid flowchart when the content is really a process. The proposal opens in the editor for your review; nothing is saved until you save it. • Works out of the box: the tool window checks the channel when it opens and shows the result as a dot in its header — green when cinder-mcp is there, red when it is not, and clicking it re-checks. Every setup step (locate the binary, start the local service) lives in the settings tree; nothing is downloaded or built, and a service you started yourself is never touched.
The plugin is a thin client: its data goes over MCP to repotory-mcp, which opens the same local database the desktop app uses, and the one thing that still speaks HTTP — moving a note between projects — talks to the loopback-only Cinder service. Everything stays on your machine — there is nothing to authenticate and nothing that leaves it. One build covers the whole IntelliJ family (IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand and the rest), on IntelliJ 2024.2 or newer, independently of your project's JDK.
